  56def equal_edges(
  57    edge1: LineType,
  58    edge2: LineType,
  59    rel_tol: float | None = None,
  60    abs_tol: float | None = None,
  61) -> bool:
  62    """Return True if two edges have matching endpoints (either orientation).
  63
  64    Args:
  65        edge1: First edge ``(p1, p2)``.
  66        edge2: Second edge ``(p3, p4)``.
  67        rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
  68        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
  69
  70    Returns:
  71        bool: True if endpoints match within ``abs_tol``.
  72
  73    Examples:
  74        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
  75        >>> sg.equal_edges([(0, 0), (40, 0)], [(40, 0), (0, 0)])
  76        True
  77        >>> sg.equal_edges([(0, 0), (40, 0)], [(0, 0), (40, 40)])
  78        False
  79    """
  80    p1, p2 = edge1
  81    p3, p4 = edge2
  82
  83    return (
  84        equal_points(p1, p3, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
  85        and equal_points(p2, p4, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
  86    ) or (
  87        equal_points(p1, p4, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
  88        and equal_points(p2, p3, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
  89    )
  90

 173def line_angle(start_point: PointType, end_point: PointType) -> float:
 174    """Return the orientation angle (in radians) of a line given by start and end points.
 175    Order makes a difference.
 176
 177    Args:
 178        start_point (PointType): Start point of the line.
 179        end_point (PointType): End point of the line.
 180
 181    Returns:
 182        float: Orientation angle of the line in radians.
 183
 184    Examples:
 185        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 186        >>> sg.line_angle((0, 0), (40, 0))
 187        0.0
 188        >>> sg.line_angle((0, 0), (0, 40)) == sg.pi / 2
 189        True
 190    """
 191    return positive_angle(
 192        atan2(end_point[1] - start_point[1], end_point[0] - start_point[0])
 193    )

 196def angled_line(line: LineType, theta: float) -> LineType:
 197    """
 198    Given a line find another line with theta radians between them.
 199
 200    Args:
 201        line (LineType): Input line.
 202        theta (float): Angle in radians.
 203
 204    Returns:
 205        LineType: New line with the given angle.
 206
 207    Examples:
 208        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 209        >>> p0, p1 = sg.angled_line([(0, 0), (40, 0)], sg.pi / 2)
 210        >>> p0, (round(p1[0], 10), round(p1[1], 10))
 211        ((0, 0), (0.0, 40.0))
 212    """
 213    # find the angle of the line
 214    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
 215    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
 216    theta1 = atan2(y2 - y1, x2 - x1)
 217    theta2 = theta1 + theta
 218    # find the length of the line
 219    dx = x2 - x1
 220    dy = y2 - y1
 221    length_ = (dx**2 + dy**2) ** 0.5
 222    # find the new line
 223    x3 = x1 + length_ * cos(theta2)
 224    y3 = y1 + length_ * sin(theta2)
 225
 226    return [(x1, y1), (x3, y3)]

 229def offset_line(
 230    line: Sequence[PointType], offset: float
 231) -> Sequence[PointType]:
 232    """Return an offset line from a given line.
 233
 234    Args:
 235        line (Sequence[PointType]): Input line.
 236        offset (float): Offset distance.
 237
 238    Returns:
 239        Sequence[PointType]: Offset line.
 240
 241    Examples:
 242        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 243        >>> sg.offset_line([(0, 0), (40, 0)], 1)
 244        [[0.0, 1.0], [40.0, 1.0]]
 245    """
 246    unit_vec = perp_unit_vector(line)
 247    dx = unit_vec[0] * offset
 248    dy = unit_vec[1] * offset
 249    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
 250    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
 251    return [[x1 + dx, y1 + dy], [x2 + dx, y2 + dy]]
 252
 253
 254def offset_lines(
 255    polylines: Sequence[LineType], offset: float = 1
 256) -> list[LineType]:
 257    """Return a list of offset lines from a list of lines.
 258
 259    Args:
 260        polylines (Sequence[LineType]): List of input lines.
 261        offset (float, optional): Offset distance. Defaults to 1.
 262
 263    Returns:
 264        list[LineType]: List of offset lines.
 265
 266    Examples:
 267        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 268        >>> sg.offset_lines([((0, 0), (80, 0)), ((80, 0), (80, 80))], 20)
 269        [([0.0, 20.0], (60.0, 20.0)), ((60.0, 20.0), [60.0, 80.0])]
 270    """
 271    offset_segs = [offset_line(line, offset) for line in polylines]
 272    points = stitch(offset_segs, closed=False, return_points=True)
 273    return connected_pairs(points)

 276def parallel_line(line: LineType, point: PointType) -> LineType:
 277    """Return a parallel line to the given line that goes through the given point
 278
 279    Args:
 280        line (LineType): Input line.
 281        point (PointType): PointType through which the parallel line passes.
 282
 283    Returns:
 284        LineType: Parallel line.
 285
 286    Examples:
 287        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 288        >>> sg.parallel_line([(0, 0), (40, 0)], (0, 80))
 289        [[0, 80], [40, 80]]
 290    """
 291    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
 292    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
 293    x3, y3 = point
 294    dx = x2 - x1
 295    dy = y2 - y1
 296    return [[x3, y3], [x3 + dx, y3 + dy]]

 299def perp_bisector(line: LineType) -> LineType:
 300    """Return the perpendicular bisector of a line
 301
 302    Args:
 303        line (LineType): Input line.
 304
 305    Returns:
 306        LineType: Perpendicular bisector of the line.
 307
 308    Examples:
 309        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 310        >>> sg.perp_bisector([(0, 0), (80, 0)])
 311        [(40.0, 0.0), [40.0, 80.0]]
 312    """
 313    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
 314    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
 315    mid = midpoint(line[0], line[1])
 316    dx = x2 - x1
 317    dy = y2 - y1
 318    return [mid, [mid[0] - dy, mid[1] + dx]]

 321def collinear3(
 322    a: PointType,
 323    b: PointType,
 324    c: PointType,
 325    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 326    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 327) -> bool:
 328    """Return True if a, b, and c are collinear.
 329
 330    Args:
 331        a (PointType): First point.
 332        b (PointType): Second point.
 333        c (PointType): Third point.
 334        rel_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance. Defaults to None.
 335        abs_tol (float, optional): Absolute tolerance. Defaults to None.
 336
 337    Returns:
 338        bool: True if the points are collinear, False otherwise.
 339
 340    Examples:
 341        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 342        >>> sg.collinear3((0, 0), (40, 40), (80, 80))
 343        True
 344        >>> sg.collinear3((0, 0), (40, 0), (0, 40))
 345        False
 346    """
 347    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 348
 349    return abs(double_area3(a, b, c)) <= abs_tol
 350

 352def merge_consecutive_collinear_edges(
 353    points: Sequence[PointType],
 354    closed: bool = False,
 355    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 356    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 357) -> list[PointType]:
 358    """Remove the middle points from collinear edges.
 359
 360    Args:
 361        points (list[PointType]): List of points.
 362        closed (bool, optional): Whether the points form a closed shape. Defaults to False.
 363        rel_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance. Defaults to None.
 364        abs_tol (float, optional): Absolute tolerance. Defaults to None.
 365
 366    Returns:
 367        list[PointType]: List of points with collinear points removed.
 368
 369    Examples:
 370        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import merge_consecutive_collinear_edges
 371        >>> merge_consecutive_collinear_edges([(0, 0), (40, 0), (80, 0), (80, 40)])
 372        [(0, 0), (80, 0), (80, 40)]
 373    """
 374    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 375    points = points[:]
 376
 377    while True:
 378        cyc = cycle(points)
 379        a = next(cyc)
 380        b = next(cyc)
 381        c = next(cyc)
 382        looping = False
 383        n = len(points) - 1
 384        if closed:
 385            n += 1
 386        discarded = []
 387        for _ in range(n - 1):
 388            if collinear3(
 389                a,
 390                b,
 391                c,
 392                rel_tol=rel_tol,
 393                abs_tol=abs_tol,
 394            ):
 395                discarded.append(b)
 396                looping = True
 397                break
 398            a = b
 399            b = c
 400            c = next(cyc)
 401        for point in discarded:
 402            points.remove(point)
 403        if not looping or len(points) < 3:
 404            break
 405
 406    return points

 409def round_segment(segment: Sequence[PointType], n_digits: int = 2) -> LineType:
 410    """Round a segment to a given precision.
 411
 412    Args:
 413        segment (Sequence[PointType]): Input segment.
 414        n_digits (int, optional): Number of decimal places to round to. Defaults to 2.
 415
 416    Returns:
 417        Sequence[PointType]: Rounded segment.
 418
 419    Examples:
 420        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 421        >>> sg.round_segment([(1.26, 2.34), (3.56, 4.78)], 1)
 422        [(1.3, 2.3), (3.6, 4.8)]
 423    """
 424    p1 = round_point(segment[0], n_digits)
 425    p2 = round_point(segment[1], n_digits)
 426
 427    return [p1, p2]

 430def line_segment_bbox(
 431    x1: float, y1: float, x2: float, y2: float
 432) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
 433    """
 434    Return the bounding box of a line segment.
 435
 436    Args:
 437        x1 (float): Segment start point x-coordinate.
 438        y1 (float): Segment start point y-coordinate.
 439        x2 (float): Segment end point x-coordinate.
 440        y2 (float): Segment end point y-coordinate.
 441
 442    Returns:
 443        tuple: Bounding box as (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y).
 444
 445    Examples:
 446        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 447        >>> sg.line_segment_bbox(40, 80, 80, 0)
 448        (40, 0, 80, 80)
 449    """
 450    return (min(x1, x2), min(y1, y2), max(x1, x2), max(y1, y2))
 451

 453def line_segment_bbox_check(seg1: LineType, seg2: LineType) -> bool:
 454    """
 455    Given two line segments, return True if their bounding boxes overlap.
 456
 457    Args:
 458        seg1 (LineType): First line segment.
 459        seg2 (LineType): Second line segment.
 460
 461    Returns:
 462        bool: True if the bounding boxes overlap, False otherwise.
 463
 464    Examples:
 465        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 466        >>> sg.line_segment_bbox_check([(0, 0), (80, 0)], [(40, -40), (40, 40)])
 467        True
 468    """
 469    x1, y1 = seg1[0][:2]
 470    x2, y2 = seg1[1][:2]
 471    x3, y3 = seg2[0][:2]
 472    x4, y4 = seg2[1][:2]
 473    return bbox_overlap(
 474        *line_segment_bbox(x1, y1, x2, y2), *line_segment_bbox(x3, y3, x4, y4)
 475    )

 478def intersect2(
 479    x1: float,
 480    y1: float,
 481    x2: float,
 482    y2: float,
 483    x3: float,
 484    y3: float,
 485    x4: float,
 486    y4: float,
 487    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 488    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 489) -> PointType:
 490    """Return the intersection point of two lines.
 491    line1: (x1, y1), (x2, y2)
 492    line2: (x3, y3), (x4, y4)
 493    To find the intersection point of two line segments use the
 494    "intersection" function
 495
 496    Args:
 497        x1 (float): x-coordinate of the first point of the first line.
 498        y1 (float): y-coordinate of the first point of the first line.
 499        x2 (float): x-coordinate of the second point of the first line.
 500        y2 (float): y-coordinate of the second point of the first line.
 501        x3 (float): x-coordinate of the first point of the second line.
 502        y3 (float): y-coordinate of the first point of the second line.
 503        x4 (float): x-coordinate of the second point of the second line.
 504        y4 (float): y-coordinate of the second point of the second line.
 505        rel_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance. Defaults to None.
 506        abs_tol (float, optional): Absolute tolerance. Defaults to None.
 507
 508    Returns:
 509        PointType: Intersection point of the two lines.
 510
 511    Examples:
 512        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 513        >>> sg.intersect2(0, 0, 80, 80, 0, 80, 80, 0)
 514        (40.0, 40.0)
 515    """
 516    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
 517    x1_x2 = x1 - x2
 518    y1_y2 = y1 - y2
 519    x3_x4 = x3 - x4
 520    y3_y4 = y3 - y4
 521
 522    denom = (x1_x2) * (y3_y4) - (y1_y2) * (x3_x4)
 523    if isclose(denom, 0, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol):
 524        res = None  # parallel lines
 525    else:
 526        x = (
 527            (x1 * y2 - y1 * x2) * (x3_x4) - (x1_x2) * (x3 * y4 - y3 * x4)
 528        ) / denom
 529        y = (
 530            (x1 * y2 - y1 * x2) * (y3_y4) - (y1_y2) * (x3 * y4 - y3 * x4)
 531        ) / denom
 532        res = (x, y)
 533
 534    return res
 535

 537def intersect(line1: LineType, line2: LineType) -> PointType:
 538    """Return the intersection point of two lines.
 539    line1: [(x1, y1), (x2, y2)]
 540    line2: [(x3, y3), (x4, y4)]
 541    To find the intersection point of two line segments use the
 542    "intersection" function
 543
 544    Args:
 545        line1 (LineType): First line.
 546        line2 (LineType): Second line.
 547
 548    Returns:
 549        PointType: Intersection point of the two lines.
 550
 551    Examples:
 552        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 553        >>> sg.intersect([(0, 0), (80, 80)], [(0, 80), (80, 0)])
 554        (40.0, 40.0)
 555    """
 556    x1, y1 = line1[0][:2]
 557    x2, y2 = line1[1][:2]
 558    x3, y3 = line2[0][:2]
 559    x4, y4 = line2[1][:2]
 560    return intersect2(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4)
 561

 563def segment_connection(
 564    x1: float,
 565    y1: float,
 566    x2: float,
 567    y2: float,
 568    x3: float,
 569    y3: float,
 570    x4: float,
 571    y4: float,
 572    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 573    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 574) -> tuple[Connection, PointType | None]:
 575    """Return the connection kind and crossing point of two segments.
 576
 577    Args:
 578        x1 (float): x-coordinate of the first point of the first line segment.
 579        y1 (float): y-coordinate of the first point of the first line segment.
 580        x2 (float): x-coordinate of the second point of the first line segment.
 581        y2 (float): y-coordinate of the second point of the first line segment.
 582        x3 (float): x-coordinate of the first point of the second line segment.
 583        y3 (float): y-coordinate of the first point of the second line segment.
 584        x4 (float): x-coordinate of the second point of the second line segment.
 585        y4 (float): y-coordinate of the second point of the second line segment.
 586        rel_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance. Defaults to None.
 587        abs_tol (float, optional): Absolute tolerance. Defaults to None.
 588
 589    Returns:
 590        tuple: Connection type and intersection point.
 591
 592    Examples:
 593        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 594        >>> kind, point = sg.segment_connection(0, 0, 80, 80, 0, 80, 80, 0)
 595        >>> kind == sg.Connection.INTERSECT, point
 596        (True, (40.0, 40.0))
 597        >>> kind, _ = sg.segment_connection(0, 0, 40, 0, 0, 40, 40, 40)
 598        >>> kind == sg.Connection.PARALLEL
 599        True
 600    """
 601    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
 602    x2_x1 = x2 - x1
 603    y2_y1 = y2 - y1
 604    x4_x3 = x4 - x3
 605    y4_y3 = y4 - y3
 606    denom = (y4_y3) * (x2_x1) - (x4_x3) * (y2_y1)
 607    if isclose(denom, 0, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol):  # parallel
 608        return Connection.PARALLEL, None
 609    x1_x3 = x1 - x3
 610    y1_y3 = y1 - y3
 611    ua = ((x4_x3) * (y1_y3) - (y4_y3) * (x1_x3)) / denom
 612    if ua < 0 or ua > 1:
 613        return Connection.DISJOINT, None
 614    ub = ((x2_x1) * (y1_y3) - (y2_y1) * (x1_x3)) / denom
 615    if ub < 0 or ub > 1:
 616        return Connection.DISJOINT, None
 617    x = x1 + ua * (x2_x1)
 618    y = y1 + ua * (y2_y1)
 619    return Connection.INTERSECT, (x, y)
 620
 621
 622def collinear_segments(
 623    segment1: LineType,
 624    segment2: LineType,
 625    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 626    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 627) -> bool:
 628    """
 629    Checks if two line segments (a1, b1) and (a2, b2) are collinear.
 630
 631    Args:
 632        segment1 (LineType): First line segment.
 633        segment2 (LineType): Second line segment.
 634        rel_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance. Defaults to None.
 635        abs_tol (float, optional): Absolute tolerance. Defaults to None.
 636
 637    Returns:
 638        bool: True if the segments are collinear, False otherwise.
 639
 640    Examples:
 641        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 642        >>> sg.collinear_segments([(0, 0), (80, 0)], [(40, 0), (60, 0)])
 643        True
 644        >>> sg.collinear_segments([(0, 0), (80, 0)], [(0, 40), (80, 40)])
 645        False
 646    """
 647    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 648    a1, b1 = segment1
 649    a2, b2 = segment2
 650
 651    return isclose(
 652        direction3(a1, b1, a2),
 653        0,
 654        rel_tol=rel_tol,
 655        abs_tol=abs_tol,
 656    ) and isclose(
 657        direction3(a1, b1, b2),
 658        0,
 659        rel_tol=rel_tol,
 660        abs_tol=abs_tol,
 661    )
 662
 663
 664def check_intersection(
 665    x1: float,
 666    y1: float,
 667    x2: float,
 668    y2: float,
 669    x3: float,
 670    y3: float,
 671    x4: float,
 672    y4: float,
 673    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 674    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 675) -> tuple[Connection, list]:
 676    """Return a fine-grained classification of how two line segments meet.
 677
 678    The result names the relationship, not only whether a crossing exists.
 679    It distinguishes a proper intersection from endpoint chains, collinear
 680    overlap, containment, congruent segments, and Y-joints.
 681
 682    Args:
 683        x1 (float): x-coordinate of the first point of the first line segment.
 684        y1 (float): y-coordinate of the first point of the first line segment.
 685        x2 (float): x-coordinate of the second point of the first line segment.
 686        y2 (float): y-coordinate of the second point of the first line segment.
 687        x3 (float): x-coordinate of the first point of the second line segment.
 688        y3 (float): y-coordinate of the first point of the second line segment.
 689        x4 (float): x-coordinate of the second point of the second line segment.
 690        y4 (float): y-coordinate of the second point of the second line segment.
 691        rel_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance. Defaults to None.
 692        abs_tol (float, optional): Absolute tolerance. Defaults to None.
 693
 694    Returns:
 695        tuple[Connection, PointType | Sequence | None]: A ``Connection``
 696        kind and the geometry for that kind. The second value is a point
 697        for a crossing or joint, a segment for overlap or containment,
 698        or ``None`` when the segments are disjoint or parallel and do not meet.
 699
 700    Examples:
 701        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 702        >>> kind, point = sg.check_intersection(0, 0, 80, 80, 0, 80, 80, 0)
 703        >>> kind == sg.Connection.INTERSECT, point
 704        (True, (40.0, 40.0))
 705    """
 706    # collinear check uses area tolerances
 707
 708    # s1: start1 = (x1, y1)
 709    # e1: end1 = (x2, y2)
 710    # s2: start2 = (x3, y3)
 711    # e2: end2 = (x4, y4)
 712    # s1s2: start1 and start2 is connected
 713    # s1e2: start1 and end2 is connected
 714    # e1s2: end1 and start2 is connected
 715    # e1e2: end1 and end2 is connected
 716    rel_tol, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
 717    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
 718
 719    s1 = (x1, y1)
 720    e1 = (x2, y2)
 721    s2 = (x3, y3)
 722    e2 = (x4, y4)
 723    segment1 = [(x1, y1), (x2, y2)]
 724    segment2 = [(x3, y3), (x4, y4)]
 725
 726    # check if the segments' bounding boxes overlap
 727    if not line_segment_bbox_check(segment1, segment2):
 728        return (Connection.DISJOINT, None)
 729
 730    # Check if the segments are parallel
 731    x2_x1 = x2 - x1
 732    y2_y1 = y2 - y1
 733    x4_x3 = x4 - x3
 734    y4_y3 = y4 - y3
 735    denom = (y4_y3) * (x2_x1) - (x4_x3) * (y2_y1)
 736    parallel = isclose(denom, 0, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
 737    # angle1 = atan2(y2 - y1, x2 - x1) % pi
 738    # angle2 = atan2(y4 - y3, x4 - x3) % pi
 739    # parallel = close_angles(angle1, angle2, abs_tol=defaults['abs_tol'])
 740
 741    # Coincident end points
 742    s1s2 = close_points_square(s1, s2, dist2=abs_tol2)
 743    s1e2 = close_points_square(s1, e2, dist2=abs_tol2)
 744    e1s2 = close_points_square(e1, s2, dist2=abs_tol2)
 745    e1e2 = close_points_square(e1, e2, dist2=abs_tol2)
 746    connected = s1s2 or s1e2 or e1s2 or e1e2
 747    if parallel:
 748        length1 = distance((x1, y1), (x2, y2))
 749        length2 = distance((x3, y3), (x4, y4))
 750        min_x = min(x1, x2, x3, x4)
 751        max_x = max(x1, x2, x3, x4)
 752        min_y = min(y1, y2, y3, y4)
 753        max_y = max(y1, y2, y3, y4)
 754        total_length = distance((min_x, min_y), (max_x, max_y))
 755        l1_eq_l2 = isclose(length1, length2, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol)
 756        l1_eq_total = isclose(
 757            length1, total_length, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol
 758        )
 759        l2_eq_total = isclose(
 760            length2, total_length, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol
 761        )
 762        if connected:
 763            if l1_eq_l2 and l1_eq_total:
 764                return Connection.CONGRUENT, segment1
 765
 766            if l1_eq_total:
 767                return Connection.CONTAINS, segment1
 768            if l2_eq_total:
 769                return Connection.WITHIN, segment2
 770            if isclose(
 771                length1 + length2,
 772                total_length,
 773                rel_tol=rel_tol,
 774                abs_tol=abs_tol,
 775            ):
 776                # chained and collienar
 777                if s1s2:
 778                    return Connection.COLL_CHAIN, (e1, s1, e2)
 779                if s1e2:
 780                    return Connection.COLL_CHAIN, (e1, s1, s2)
 781                if e1s2:
 782                    return Connection.COLL_CHAIN, (s1, s2, e2)
 783                if e1e2:
 784                    return Connection.COLL_CHAIN, (s1, e1, s2)
 785        else:
 786            if total_length < length1 + length2 and collinear_segments(
 787                segment1,
 788                segment2,
 789                rel_tol=rel_tol,
 790                abs_tol=abs_tol,
 791            ):
 792                p1 = (min_x, min_y)
 793                p2 = (max_x, max_y)
 794                seg = [p1, p2]
 795                return Connection.OVERLAPS, seg
 796
 797            return segment_connection(
 798                x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4, rel_tol, abs_tol
 799            )
 800    else:
 801        if connected:
 802            if s1s2:
 803                return Connection.CHAIN, (e1, s1, e2)
 804            if s1e2:
 805                return Connection.CHAIN, (e1, s1, s2)
 806            if e1s2:
 807                return Connection.CHAIN, (s1, s2, e2)
 808            if e1e2:
 809                return Connection.CHAIN, (s1, e1, s2)
 810        else:
 811            if between3(s1, e1, e2):
 812                return Connection.YJOINT, e1
 813            if between3(s1, e1, s2):
 814                return Connection.YJOINT, s1
 815            if between3(s2, e2, e1):
 816                return Connection.YJOINT, e2
 817            if between3(s2, e2, s1):
 818                return Connection.YJOINT, s2
 819
 820            return segment_connection(
 821                x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4, rel_tol, abs_tol
 822            )
 823    return (Connection.DISJOINT, None)
 824

 826def inclination_angle(start_point: PointType, end_point: PointType) -> float:
 827    """Return the inclination angle (in radians) of a line given by start and end points.
 828    Inclination angle is always between zero and pi.
 829    Order makes no difference.
 830
 831    Args:
 832        start_point (PointType): Start point of the line.
 833        end_point (PointType): End point of the line.
 834
 835    Returns:
 836        float: Inclination angle of the line in radians.
 837
 838    Examples:
 839        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
 840        >>> sg.inclination_angle((0, 0), (40, 40)) == sg.pi / 4
 841        True
 842        >>> sg.inclination_angle((40, 40), (0, 0)) == sg.pi / 4
 843        True
 844    """
 845    return line_angle(start_point, end_point) % pi
 846

 848def clip_line_to_rect(
 849    point: PointType,
 850    direction: PointType,
 851    lower_left: PointType,
 852    upper_right: PointType,
 853) -> LineType | None:
 854    """Clip an infinite line against an axis-aligned rectangle.
 855
 856    The line is defined by a point and a direction vector.
 857
 858    Args:
 859        point: A point on the line ``(x, y)``.
 860        direction: Direction vector ``(dx, dy)``.
 861        lower_left: Rectangle lower-left corner.
 862        upper_right: Rectangle upper-right corner.
 863
 864    Returns:
 865        tuple | None: Clipped segment ``((x1, y1), (x2, y2))``, or None if
 866        the line misses the rectangle.
 867
 868    Examples:
 869        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import clip_line_to_rect
 870        >>> clip_line_to_rect((0, 0), (40, 40), (0, 0), (80, 80))
 871        ((0.0, 0.0), (80.0, 80.0))
 872        >>> clip_line_to_rect((0, 100), (40, 0), (0, 0), (80, 80)) is None
 873        True
 874    """
 875    x_min, y_min = lower_left[:2]
 876    x_max, y_max = upper_right[:2]
 877    rectangle = (x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max)
 878    t_min, t_max = -float("inf"), float("inf")
 879
 880    # Iterate over x and y dimensions
 881    for i in range(2):
 882        if direction[i] == 0:
 883            if point[i] < rectangle[i] or point[i] > rectangle[i + 2]:
 884                return None
 885        else:
 886            t1 = (rectangle[i] - point[i]) / direction[i]
 887            t2 = (rectangle[i + 2] - point[i]) / direction[i]
 888            t_min = max(t_min, min(t1, t2))
 889            t_max = min(t_max, max(t1, t2))
 890
 891    if t_min <= t_max:
 892        start = (
 893            point[0] + t_min * direction[0],
 894            point[1] + t_min * direction[1],
 895        )
 896        end = (point[0] + t_max * direction[0], point[1] + t_max * direction[1])
 897        return (start, end)
 898    return None
 899

 901def sorted_edges(polygon: Sequence[PointType]) -> list[LineType]:
 902    """Return polygon edges sorted for sweep-line processing.
 903
 904    Edges are oriented left-to-right, then sorted by increasing start ``x``
 905    and ``y``. Used by simplicity tests.
 906
 907    Args:
 908        polygon: Sequence of polygon vertices.
 909
 910    Returns:
 911        list: Oriented and sorted edges ``[(p1, p2), ...]``.
 912
 913    Examples:
 914        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import sorted_edges
 915        >>> sorted_edges([(40, 40), (0, 0), (80, 0)])
 916        [((0, 0), (40, 40)), ((0, 0), (80, 0)), ((40, 40), (80, 0))]
 917    """
 918
 919    # order the edges:increasing x coordinates then increasing y coordinates for the start points
 920    # this is used for line sweep algorithm to check if the polygon is simple
 921    def compare_edges(edge1: LineType, edge2: LineType) -> int:
 922        x1 = edge1[0][0]
 923        x2 = edge2[0][0]
 924        y1 = edge1[0][1]
 925        y2 = edge2[0][1]
 926        if x1 < x2:
 927            return -1
 928        elif x1 > x2:
 929            return 1
 930        else:
 931            if y1 < y2:
 932                return -1
 933            elif y1 > y2:
 934                return 1
 935            else:
 936                return 0
 937
 938    edges = connected_pairs(polygon, closed=True)
 939    oriented_edges = []
 940    for edge in edges:
 941        start_x, start_y = edge[0][:2]
 942        end_x, end_y = edge[1][:2]
 943        if start_x > end_x or (start_x == end_x and start_y > end_y):
 944            oriented_edges.append((edge[1], edge[0]))
 945        else:
 946            oriented_edges.append(edge)
 947    oriented_edges.sort(key=cmp_to_key(compare_edges))
 948
 949    return oriented_edges
 950
 951
 952def all_intersections(
 953    edges: list[tuple[PointType, PointType]],
 954    rel_tol: float | None = None,
 955    abs_tol: float | None = None,
 956    return_points_list: bool = False,
 957) -> tuple[dict, list[tuple]]:
 958    """Return all proper intersections between the given edges.
 959
 960    Bounding-box candidates are collected into one NumPy array, then
 961    line-segment intersections are computed in bulk.
 962
 963    Args:
 964        edges: Line segments to test.
 965        rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to settings default.
 966        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to settings default.
 967        return_points_list: If True, include a flat list of intersection
 968            points in the return value.
 969
 970    Returns:
 971        tuple: ``(intersection_map, points)`` when ``return_points_list``
 972        is True; otherwise an intersection map keyed by edge id.
 973
 974    Examples:
 975        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import all_intersections
 976        >>> _, points = all_intersections([((0, 0), (80, 80)), ((0, 80), (80, 0))])
 977        >>> len(points)
 978        1
 979        >>> float(points[0][0]), float(points[0][1])
 980        (40.0, 40.0)
 981    """
 982
 983    relative_tolerance, absolute_tolerance = get_defaults(
 984        ["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol]
 985    )
 986    edge_coordinates = []
 987    for edge in edges:
 988        start_point, end_point = edge
 989        start_x, start_y = start_point[:2]
 990        end_x, end_y = end_point[:2]
 991        edge_coordinates.append([start_x, start_y, end_x, end_y])
 992
 993    edge_array = np.asarray(edge_coordinates, dtype=float)
 994    edge_count = edge_array.shape[0]
 995    edge_min_x = np.minimum(edge_array[:, 0], edge_array[:, 2])
 996    edge_min_y = np.minimum(edge_array[:, 1], edge_array[:, 3])
 997    edge_max_x = np.maximum(edge_array[:, 0], edge_array[:, 2])
 998    edge_max_y = np.maximum(edge_array[:, 1], edge_array[:, 3])
 999    edge_ids = np.arange(edge_count)
1000    sort_order = edge_min_x.argsort()
1001    edge_array = edge_array[sort_order]
1002    edge_min_x = edge_min_x[sort_order]
1003    edge_min_y = edge_min_y[sort_order]
1004    edge_max_x = edge_max_x[sort_order]
1005    edge_max_y = edge_max_y[sort_order]
1006    edge_ids = edge_ids[sort_order]
1007
1008    candidate_starts = np.arange(edge_count) + 1
1009    candidate_ends = np.searchsorted(edge_min_x, edge_max_x, side="right")
1010    candidate_counts = candidate_ends - candidate_starts
1011    candidate_count = candidate_counts.sum()
1012    if not candidate_count:
1013        if return_points_list:
1014            return []
1015        return {}, []
1016
1017    candidate_offsets = np.cumsum(candidate_counts) - candidate_counts
1018    candidate_rows = np.arange(candidate_count)
1019    first_indices = np.repeat(np.arange(edge_count), candidate_counts)
1020    candidate_offsets = np.repeat(candidate_offsets, candidate_counts)
1021    candidate_starts = np.repeat(candidate_starts, candidate_counts)
1022    second_indices = candidate_rows - candidate_offsets + candidate_starts
1023    y_overlap_mask = (
1024        edge_min_y[first_indices] <= edge_max_y[second_indices]
1025    ) & (edge_max_y[first_indices] >= edge_min_y[second_indices])
1026    first_indices = first_indices[y_overlap_mask]
1027    second_indices = second_indices[y_overlap_mask]
1028    candidate_array = np.hstack(
1029        (
1030            edge_array[first_indices],
1031            edge_array[second_indices],
1032            edge_ids[first_indices, None],
1033            edge_ids[second_indices, None],
1034        )
1035    )
1036    first_edges = candidate_array[:, :4]
1037    second_edges = candidate_array[:, 4:8]
1038    first_delta_x = first_edges[:, 2] - first_edges[:, 0]
1039    first_delta_y = first_edges[:, 3] - first_edges[:, 1]
1040    second_delta_x = second_edges[:, 2] - second_edges[:, 0]
1041    second_delta_y = second_edges[:, 3] - second_edges[:, 1]
1042    denominator = (
1043        second_delta_y * first_delta_x - second_delta_x * first_delta_y
1044    )
1045
1046    parallel_mask = np.abs(denominator) <= np.maximum(
1047        absolute_tolerance, relative_tolerance * np.abs(denominator)
1048    )
1049    candidate_array = candidate_array[~parallel_mask]
1050    first_edges = first_edges[~parallel_mask]
1051    second_edges = second_edges[~parallel_mask]
1052    first_delta_x = first_delta_x[~parallel_mask]
1053    first_delta_y = first_delta_y[~parallel_mask]
1054    second_delta_x = second_delta_x[~parallel_mask]
1055    second_delta_y = second_delta_y[~parallel_mask]
1056    denominator = denominator[~parallel_mask]
1057    first_to_second_x = first_edges[:, 0] - second_edges[:, 0]
1058    first_to_second_y = first_edges[:, 1] - second_edges[:, 1]
1059    first_parameter = (
1060        second_delta_x * first_to_second_y - second_delta_y * first_to_second_x
1061    ) / denominator
1062    second_parameter = (
1063        first_delta_x * first_to_second_y - first_delta_y * first_to_second_x
1064    ) / denominator
1065    intersecting_mask = (
1066        (first_parameter >= 0)
1067        & (first_parameter <= 1)
1068        & (second_parameter >= 0)
1069        & (second_parameter <= 1)
1070    )
1071    intersection_x = first_edges[:, 0] + first_parameter * first_delta_x
1072    intersection_y = first_edges[:, 1] + first_parameter * first_delta_y
1073    intersection_rows = candidate_array[intersecting_mask]
1074
1075    if return_points_list:
1076        res = [
1077            ((x_coordinate, y_coordinate), (int(first_id), int(second_id)))
1078            for x_coordinate, y_coordinate, first_id, second_id in zip(
1079                intersection_x[intersecting_mask],
1080                intersection_y[intersecting_mask],
1081                intersection_rows[:, 8],
1082                intersection_rows[:, 9],
1083            )
1084        ]
1085    else:
1086        d_results = {}
1087        points = []
1088        for x_coordinate, y_coordinate, first_id, second_id in zip(
1089            intersection_x[intersecting_mask],
1090            intersection_y[intersecting_mask],
1091            intersection_rows[:, 8],
1092            intersection_rows[:, 9],
1093        ):
1094            point = (x_coordinate, y_coordinate)
1095            first_id = int(first_id)
1096            second_id = int(second_id)
1097            if first_id not in d_results:
1098                d_results[first_id] = []
1099            if second_id not in d_results:
1100                d_results[second_id] = []
1101            d_results[first_id].append((point, second_id))
1102            d_results[second_id].append((point, first_id))
1103            points.append(point)
1104        res = (d_results, points)
1105
1106    return res
1107
1108
1109def all_segments_sorted(
1110    edges: list[tuple[PointType, PointType]],
1111    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1112    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1113) -> list[tuple[PointType]]:
1114    """Split edges at intersection points, ordered along each edge.
1115
1116    Intersection points on an edge are sorted by distance from the edge's
1117    first endpoint. The result is a flat list of consecutive sub-segments.
1118
1119    Args:
1120        edges: Input line segments.
1121        rel_tol: Relative tolerance for intersections.
1122        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance for intersections.
1123
1124    Returns:
1125        list: Sub-segments covering each input edge in order.
1126
1127    Examples:
1128        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import all_segments_sorted
1129        >>> segs = all_segments_sorted([((0, 0), (80, 0)), ((40, -40), (40, 40))])
1130        >>> segs
1131        [((0, 0), (40.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (80, 0)), ((40, -40), (40.0, 0.0)), ((40.0, 0.0), (40, 40))]
1132    """
1133    intersection_map, _ = all_intersections(edges, rel_tol, abs_tol)
1134
1135    intersections_by_edge = {edge_id: [] for edge_id in range(len(edges))}
1136    intersections_by_edge.update(intersection_map)
1137
1138    sorted_segments = []
1139    for edge_id, edge in enumerate(edges):
1140        start_point, end_point = edge
1141        intersections = sorted(
1142            intersections_by_edge[edge_id],
1143            key=lambda item: distance(start_point, item[0]),
1144        )
1145        points_on_edge = []
1146        point_coordinates = {tuple(start_point[:2]), tuple(end_point[:2])}
1147        for point, _ in intersections:
1148            coordinates = tuple(point[:2])
1149            if coordinates not in point_coordinates:
1150                points_on_edge.append(point)
1151                point_coordinates.add(coordinates)
1152        edge_points = [start_point] + points_on_edge + [end_point]
1153        sorted_segments.extend(connected_pairs(edge_points))
1154        # sorted_segments.append(
1155        #     tuple([start_point] + points_on_edge + [end_point])
1156
1157    return sorted_segments
1158
1159
1160def angle_between_lines3(
1161    point1: PointType, point2: PointType, point3: PointType
1162) -> float:
1163    """
1164    Given line1 as point1 and point2, and line2 as point2 and point3
1165    return the angle between two lines
1166    (point2 is the corner point)
1167
1168    Args:
1169        point1 (PointType): First point of the first line.
1170        point2 (PointType): Second point of the first line and first point of the second line.
1171        point3 (PointType): Second point of the second line.
1172
1173    Returns:
1174        float: Signed angle between the two lines in radians (-π to π).
1175
1176    Examples:
1177        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import angle_between_lines3
1178        >>> angle_between_lines3((40, 0), (0, 0), (0, 40)) == 3.141592653589793 / 2
1179        True
1180    """
1181    vec1 = v_from_points(point2, point1)
1182    vec2 = v_from_points(point2, point3)
1183    cross = v_cross(vec1, vec2)
1184    dot = v_mul(vec1, vec2)
1185    return atan2(cross, dot)
1186
1187
1188def trim_right(line: LineType, x_value: float) -> LineType | None:
1189    """
1190    Trim a line to the right at a given x-coordinate.
1191
1192    Args:
1193        line (LineType): The line to trim.
1194        x_value (float): The x-coordinate to trim the line at.
1195
1196    Returns:
1197        LineType: The trimmed line.
1198
1199    Examples:
1200        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import trim_right
1201        >>> trim_right([(0, 0), (80, 0)], 2)
1202        [(0, 0), (2.0, 0.0)]
1203    """
1204    reverse = False
1205    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
1206    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
1207    if x1 > x2:
1208        x1, x2 = x2, x1
1209        y1, y2 = y2, y1
1210        reverse = True
1211
1212    if x1 >= x_value:
1213        res = None
1214    elif x2 >= x_value:
1215        intersection_ = intersect(line, [(x_value, 0), (x_value, 1)])
1216        res = [(x1, y1), intersection_]
1217    else:
1218        res = line
1219        reverse = False
1220    if res and reverse:
1221        res = [res[1], res[0]]  # Reverse the order if we swapped x1 and x2
1222
1223    return res
1224
1225
1226def trim_left(line: LineType, x_value: float) -> LineType | None:
1227    """
1228    Trim a line to the left at a given x-coordinate.
1229
1230    Args:
1231        line (LineType): The line to trim.
1232        x_value (float): The x-coordinate to trim the line at.
1233
1234    Returns:
1235        LineType: The trimmed line.
1236
1237    Examples:
1238        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import trim_left
1239        >>> trim_left([(0, 0), (80, 0)], 2)
1240        [(2.0, 0.0), (80, 0)]
1241    """
1242    reverse = False
1243    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
1244    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
1245    if x1 > x2:
1246        x1, x2 = x2, x1
1247        y1, y2 = y2, y1
1248        reverse = True
1249
1250    if x1 >= x_value:
1251        res = line
1252        reverse = False
1253    elif x2 >= x_value:
1254        intersection_ = intersect(line, [(x_value, 0), (x_value, 1)])
1255        res = [intersection_, (x2, y2)]
1256    else:
1257        res = None
1258
1259    if res and reverse:
1260        res = [res[1], res[0]]  # Reverse the order if we swapped x1 and x2
1261
1262    return res
1263
1264
1265def trim_top(line: LineType, y_value: float) -> LineType | None:
1266    """
1267    Trim a line to the top at a given y-coordinate.
1268
1269    Args:
1270        line (LineType): The line to trim.
1271        y_value (float): The y-coordinate to trim the line at.
1272
1273    Returns:
1274        LineType: The trimmed line.
1275
1276    Examples:
1277        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import trim_top
1278        >>> p0, p1 = trim_top([(0, 0), (0, 80)], 2)
1279        >>> p0, (round(abs(p1[0]), 10), round(abs(p1[1]), 10))
1280        ((0, 0), (0.0, 2.0))
1281    """
1282    reverse = False
1283    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
1284    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
1285    if y1 > y2:
1286        y1, y2 = y2, y1
1287        x1, x2 = x2, x1
1288        reverse = True
1289
1290    if y1 >= y_value:
1291        res = None
1292    elif y2 >= y_value:
1293        intersection_ = intersect(line, [(0, y_value), (1, y_value)])
1294        res = [(x1, y1), intersection_]
1295    else:
1296        res = line
1297        reverse = False
1298
1299    if res and reverse:
1300        res = [res[1], res[0]]
1301
1302    return res

1304
1305def trim_bottom(line: LineType, y_value: float) -> LineType | None:
1306    """
1307    Trim a line to the bottom at a given y-coordinate.
1308
1309    Args:
1310        line (LineType): The line to trim.
1311        y_value (float): The y-coordinate to trim the line at.
1312
1313    Returns:
1314        LineType: The trimmed line.
1315
1316    Examples:
1317        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import trim_bottom
1318        >>> p0, p1 = trim_bottom([(0, 0), (0, 80)], 2)
1319        >>> (round(abs(p0[0]), 10), round(abs(p0[1]), 10)), p1
1320        ((0.0, 2.0), (0, 80))
1321    """
1322    reverse = False
1323    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
1324    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
1325    if y1 > y2:
1326        y1, y2 = y2, y1
1327        x1, x2 = x2, x1
1328        reverse = True
1329
1330    if y1 >= y_value:
1331        res = line
1332        reverse = False
1333    elif y2 >= y_value:
1334        intersection_ = intersect(line, [(0, y_value), (1, y_value)])
1335        res = [intersection_, (x2, y2)]
1336    else:
1337        res = None
1338
1339    if res and reverse:
1340        res = [res[1], res[0]]
1341
1342    return res

1344
1345def stitch(
1346    lines: list[LineType],
1347    closed: bool = True,
1348    return_points: bool = True,
1349    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1350    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1351) -> list[PointType]:
1352    """
1353    Stitches a list of lines together.
1354
1355    Args:
1356        lines (list[LineType]): List of lines to stitch.
1357        closed (bool, optional): Whether the lines form a closed shape. Defaults to True.
1358        return_points (bool, optional): Whether to return points or lines. Defaults to True.
1359        rel_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance. Defaults to None.
1360        abs_tol (float, optional): Absolute tolerance. Defaults to None.
1361
1362    Returns:
1363        list[PointType]: Stitched list of points or lines.
1364
1365    Examples:
1366        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import stitch
1367        >>> stitch([((0, 0), (80, 0)), ((80, 0), (80, 80))], closed=False)
1368        [(0, 0), (80.0, 0.0), (80, 80)]
1369    """
1370    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
1371    if closed:
1372        points = []
1373    else:
1374        points = [lines[0][0]]
1375    for i, line in enumerate(lines[:-1]):
1376        x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
1377        x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
1378        x3, y3 = lines[i + 1][0][:2]
1379        x4, y4 = lines[i + 1][1][:2]
1380        x_point = intersect2(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4)
1381        if x_point:
1382            points.append(x_point)
1383    if closed:
1384        x1, y1 = lines[-1][0][:2]
1385        x2, y2 = lines[-1][1][:2]
1386        x3, y3 = lines[0][0][:2]
1387        x4, y4 = lines[0][1][:2]
1388        final_x = intersect2(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4)
1389        if final_x:
1390            points.insert(0, final_x)
1391            points.append(final_x)
1392    else:
1393        points.append(lines[-1][1])
1394    if return_points:
1395        res = points
1396    else:
1397        res = connected_pairs(points)
1398
1399    return res
1400
1401
1402def equal_lines(
1403    line1: LineType,
1404    line2: LineType,
1405    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1406    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1407) -> bool:
1408    """
1409    Return True if two lines are close enough.
1410
1411    Args:
1412        line1 (LineType): First line.
1413        line2 (LineType): Second line.
1414        rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
1415        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
1416
1417    Returns:
1418        bool: True if the lines are close enough, False otherwise.
1419
1420    Examples:
1421        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1422        >>> sg.equal_lines([(0, 0), (40, 0)], [(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1423        True
1424    """
1425    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
1426    abs_tol2 = abs_tol * abs_tol
1427    p1, p2 = line1
1428    p3, p4 = line2
1429    return (
1430        close_points_square(p1, p3, dist2=abs_tol2)
1431        and close_points_square(p2, p4, dist2=abs_tol2)
1432    ) or (
1433        close_points_square(p1, p4, dist2=abs_tol2)
1434        and close_points_square(p2, p3, dist2=abs_tol2)
1435    )
1436
1437
1438def length(line: LineType) -> float:
1439    """Return the length of a line.
1440
1441    Args:
1442        line (LineType): Input line.
1443
1444    Returns:
1445        float: Length of the line.
1446
1447    Examples:
1448        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1449        >>> sg.length(((0, 0), (60, 80)))
1450        100.0
1451    """
1452    p1, p2 = line
1453    return distance(p1, p2)
1454
1455
1456def extended_line(
1457    dist: float, line: LineType, extend_both: bool = False
1458) -> LineType:
1459    """
1460    Given a line ((x1, y1), (x2, y2)) and a distance,
1461    the given line is extended by distance units.
1462    Return a new line ((x1, y1), (x2', y2')).
1463
1464    Args:
1465        dist (float): Distance to extend the line.
1466        line (LineType): Input line.
1467        extend_both (bool, optional): Whether to extend both ends of the line. Defaults to False.
1468
1469    Returns:
1470        LineType: Extended line.
1471
1472    Examples:
1473        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import extended_line
1474        >>> extended_line(1, [(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1475        [(0, 0), (41.0, 0.0)]
1476    """
1477    start, end = line
1478    new_end = extend(start, end, length(line) + dist)
1479    if extend_both:
1480        new_start = extend(new_end, start, length((new_end, start)) + dist)
1481        res = [new_start, new_end]
1482    else:
1483        res = [start[:2], new_end]
1484
1485    return res
1486
1487
1488def line_through_point_angle(
1489    point: PointType, angle: float, length_: float, both_sides: bool = False
1490) -> LineType:
1491    """
1492    Return a line that passes through the given point
1493    with the given angle and length.
1494    If both_side is True, the line is extended on both sides by the given
1495    length.
1496
1497    Args:
1498        point (PointType): PointType through which the line passes.
1499        angle (float): Angle of the line in radians.
1500        length_ (float): Length of the line.
1501        both_sides (bool, optional): Whether to extend the line on both sides. Defaults to False.
1502
1503    Returns:
1504        LineType: Line passing through the given point with the given angle and length.
1505
1506    Examples:
1507        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import line_through_point_angle
1508        >>> line_through_point_angle((0, 0), 0, 1)
1509        [(0, 0), (1.0, 0.0)]
1510    """
1511    x, y = point[:2]
1512    line = [(x, y), (x + length_ * cos(angle), y + length_ * sin(angle))]
1513    if both_sides:
1514        p1, p2 = line
1515        line = extended_line(length_, [p2, p1])
1516
1517    return line
1518
1519
1520def split_segment(segment: LineType, point: PointType) -> list[LineType] | None:
1521    """Split a segment into two pieces at ``point``.
1522
1523    Args:
1524        segment: Line segment ``(p1, p2)``.
1525        point: Split point (must lie on the segment, not at an endpoint).
1526
1527    Returns:
1528        tuple | None: ``((p1, point), (point, p2))``, or None if ``point``
1529        is an endpoint or not on the segment.
1530
1531    Examples:
1532        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import split_segment
1533        >>> split_segment(((0, 0), (80, 0)), (40, 0))
1534        [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (80, 0))]
1535        >>> split_segment(((0, 0), (80, 0)), (0, 0)) is None
1536        True
1537    """
1538    p1, p2 = segment
1539    if close_points_square(point, p1) or close_points_square(point, p2):
1540        return None
1541    if not point_on_line_segment(point, segment):
1542        return None
1543
1544    return [(p1, point), (point, p2)]
1545
1546
1547def multi_split_segment(
1548    segment: LineType,
1549    points: Sequence[PointType],
1550    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1551    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1552) -> list[LineType] | None:
1553    """Split a segment into multiple pieces at the given points.
1554
1555    Split points are ordered by distance from the segment start.
1556
1557    Args:
1558        segment: Line segment ``(p1, p2)``.
1559        points: Points that lie on the segment.
1560        rel_tol: Relative tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]``.
1561        abs_tol: Absolute tolerance. Defaults to ``runtime_defaults["abs_tol"]``.
1562
1563    Returns:
1564        list: Consecutive sub-segments from start to end.
1565
1566    Examples:
1567        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1568        >>> sg.multi_split_segment(((0, 0), (80, 0)), [(40, 0), (60, 0)])
1569        [((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (60, 0))]
1570    """
1571    _, abs_tol = resolve_tol(rel_tol, abs_tol)
1572    p1, p2 = segment
1573    distances = []
1574    for i, pnt in enumerate(points):
1575        dist = distance(p1, pnt)
1576        distances.append((dist, i))
1577    distances.sort()
1578    points = [points[ind] for (_, ind) in distances]
1579
1580    if len(points) == 2:
1581        close_p1 = close_points_square(points[0], p1)
1582        close_p2 = close_points_square(points[1], p2)
1583        if close_p1 and close_p2:
1584            return [segment]
1585
1586    for i, pnt in enumerate(points):
1587        if close_points_square(p1, pnt):
1588            continue
1589        if not point_on_line_segment(pnt, segment):
1590            print("point not on line")
1591            return None
1592
1593    segments = []
1594    start = p1
1595    for point in points:
1596        if distance(start, point) < abs_tol:
1597            continue
1598        segments.append((start, point))
1599        start = point
1600
1601    return segments
1602
1603
1604def intersects(seg1: LineType, seg2: LineType) -> bool:
1605    """Checks if the line segments intersect.
1606    If they are chained together, they are considered as intersecting.
1607    Returns True if the segments intersect, False otherwise.
1608
1609    Args:
1610        seg1 (LineType): First line segment.
1611        seg2 (LineType): Second line segment.
1612
1613    Returns:
1614        bool: True if the segments intersect, False otherwise.
1615
1616    Examples:
1617        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import intersects
1618        >>> intersects(((0, 0), (80, 80)), ((0, 80), (80, 0)))
1619        True
1620        >>> intersects(((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((0, 40), (40, 40)))
1621        False
1622    """
1623    p1, q1 = seg1
1624    p2, q2 = seg2
1625    o1 = clockwise3(p1, q1, p2)
1626    o2 = clockwise3(p1, q1, q2)
1627    o3 = clockwise3(p2, q2, p1)
1628    o4 = clockwise3(p2, q2, q1)
1629
1630    if o1 != o2 and o3 != o4:
1631        return True
1632
1633    if o1 == 0 and between3(p1, p2, q1):
1634        return True
1635    if o2 == 0 and between3(p1, q2, q1):
1636        return True
1637    if o3 == 0 and between3(p2, p1, q2):
1638        return True
1639    return bool(o4 == 0 and between3(p2, q1, q2))
1640
1641
1642def is_chained(seg1: LineType, seg2: LineType) -> bool:
1643    """Checks if the line segments are chained together.
1644
1645    Args:
1646        seg1 (LineType): First line segment.
1647        seg2 (LineType): Second line segment.
1648
1649    Returns:
1650        bool: True if the segments are chained together, False otherwise.
1651
1652    Examples:
1653        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import is_chained
1654        >>> is_chained(((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((40, 0), (80, 0)))
1655        True
1656        >>> is_chained(((0, 0), (40, 0)), ((0, 40), (40, 40)))
1657        False
1658    """
1659    p1, q1 = seg1
1660    p2, q2 = seg2
1661    return bool(
1662        close_points_square(p1, p2)
1663        or close_points_square(p1, q2)
1664        or close_points_square(q1, p2)
1665        or close_points_square(q1, q2)
1666    )
1667
1668
1669def stitch_lines(line1: LineType, line2: LineType) -> Sequence[LineType]:
1670    """if the lines intersect, trim the lines
1671    if the lines don't intersect, extend the lines
1672
1673    Args:
1674        line1 (LineType): First line.
1675        line2 (LineType): Second line.
1676
1677    Returns:
1678        Sequence[LineType]: Trimmed or extended lines.
1679
1680    Examples:
1681        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import stitch_lines
1682        >>> stitch_lines(((0, 0), (80, 0)), ((40, -40), (40, 40)))
1683        ([(0, 0), (40.0, 0.0)], [(40.0, 0.0), (40, 40)])
1684    """
1685    intersection_ = intersect(line1, line2)
1686    res = None
1687    if intersection_:
1688        p1, _ = line1
1689        _, p2 = line2
1690        line1 = [p1, intersection_]
1691        line2 = [intersection_, p2]
1692
1693        res = (line1, line2)
1694
1695    return res
1696
1697
1698def intersection(
1699    line1: LineType, line2: LineType, rel_tol: float | None = None
1700) -> int:
1701    """return the intersection point of two line segments.
1702    segment1: ((x1, y1), (x2, y2))
1703    segment2: ((x3, y3), (x4, y4))
1704    To find the intersection point of two lines use the "intersect" function
1705
1706    Args:
1707        line1 (LineType): First line segment.
1708        line2 (LineType): Second line segment.
1709        rel_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance. Defaults to None.
1710
1711    Returns:
1712        int: Intersection type.
1713
1714    Examples:
1715        >>> from simetri.base.all_enums import Connection
1716        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import intersection
1717        >>> kind, point = intersection(((0, 0), (80, 80)), ((0, 80), (80, 0)))
1718        >>> kind == Connection.INTERSECT, point
1719        (True, (40.0, 40.0))
1720    """
1721    if rel_tol is None:
1722        rel_tol = runtime_defaults["rel_tol"]
1723    x1, y1 = line1[0][:2]
1724    x2, y2 = line1[1][:2]
1725    x3, y3 = line2[0][:2]
1726    x4, y4 = line2[1][:2]
1727    return segment_connection(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4)
1728
1729
1730def merge_segments(
1731    seg1: Sequence[PointType], seg2: Sequence[PointType]
1732) -> Sequence[PointType] | None:
1733    """Merge two segments into one if they overlap or chain.
1734
1735    Order of endpoints does not matter. Unconnected segments are not merged.
1736
1737    Args:
1738        seg1: First segment ``(p1, p2)``.
1739        seg2: Second segment ``(p3, p4)``.
1740
1741    Returns:
1742        Sequence[PointType] | None: Merged segment endpoints, or ``None`` if
1743        they cannot be merged.
1744
1745    Examples:
1746        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1747        >>> sg.merge_segments([(0, 0), (80, 0)], [(80, 0), (80, 0)])
1748        ((0, 0), (80, 0))
1749    """
1750    (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = seg1[0][:2], seg1[1][:2]
1751    (x3, y3), (x4, y4) = seg2[0][:2], seg2[1][:2]
1752    conn_type, verts = check_intersection(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, x4, y4)
1753    if conn_type in (
1754        Connection.OVERLAPS,
1755        Connection.CONGRUENT,
1756        Connection.CONTAINS,
1757        Connection.WITHIN,
1758    ):
1759        return (verts[0], verts[1])
1760    if conn_type == Connection.COLL_CHAIN:
1761        return (verts[0], verts[2])
1762    return None
1763
1764
1765def is_horizontal(line: LineType, eps: float = 0.0001) -> bool:
1766    """Return True if the line is horizontal.
1767
1768    Args:
1769        line (LineType): Input line.
1770        eps (float, optional): Tolerance. Defaults to 0.0001.
1771
1772    Returns:
1773        bool: True if the line is horizontal, False otherwise.
1774
1775    Examples:
1776        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import is_horizontal
1777        >>> is_horizontal([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1778        True
1779        >>> is_horizontal([(0, 0), (0, 40)])
1780        False
1781    """
1782    return abs(j_vec.dot(line_vector(line))) <= eps
1783
1784
1785def is_vertical(line: LineType, eps: float = 0.0001) -> bool:
1786    """Return True if the line is vertical.
1787
1788    Args:
1789        line (LineType): Input line.
1790        eps (float, optional): Tolerance. Defaults to 0.0001.
1791
1792    Returns:
1793        bool: True if the line is vertical, False otherwise.
1794
1795    Examples:
1796        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import is_vertical
1797        >>> is_vertical([(0, 0), (0, 40)])
1798        True
1799        >>> is_vertical([(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1800        False
1801    """
1802    return abs(i_vec.dot(line_vector(line))) <= eps
1803
1804
1805def slope(
1806    start_point: PointType,
1807    end_point: PointType,
1808    rel_tol: float | None = None,
1809    abs_tol: float | None = None,
1810) -> float:
1811    """Return the slope of a line given by two points.
1812    Order makes a difference.
1813
1814    Args:
1815        start_point (PointType): Start point of the line.
1816        end_point (PointType): End point of the line.
1817        rel_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance. Defaults to None.
1818        abs_tol (float, optional): Absolute tolerance. Defaults to None.
1819
1820    Returns:
1821        float: Slope of the line.
1822
1823    Examples:
1824        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import slope
1825        >>> slope((0, 0), (40, 40))
1826        1.0
1827    """
1828    rel_tol, abs_tol = get_defaults(["rel_tol", "abs_tol"], [rel_tol, abs_tol])
1829    x1, y1 = start_point[:2]
1830    x2, y2 = end_point[:2]
1831    if isclose(x1, x2, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=abs_tol):
1832        res = runtime_defaults["INF"]
1833    else:
1834        res = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)
1835
1836    return res
1837

1839def segmentize_line(line: LineType, segment_length: float) -> list[LineType]:
1840    """Return a list of points that would form segments with the given length.
1841
1842    Args:
1843        line (LineType): Input line.
1844        segment_length (float): Length of each segment.
1845
1846    Returns:
1847        list[LineType]: List of segments.
1848
1849    Examples:
1850        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import segmentize_line
1851        >>> pts = segmentize_line([(0, 0), (80, 0)], 1)
1852        >>> [[round(c, 10) for c in p[:2]] for p in pts]
1853        [[0.0, 0.0], [1.0126582278, 0.0], [2.0253164557, 0.0], [3.0379746835, 0.0], [4.0506329114, 0.0], [5.0632911392, 0.0], [6.0759493671, 0.0], [7.0886075949, 0.0], [8.1012658228, 0.0], [9.1139240506, 0.0], [10.1265822785, 0.0], [11.1392405063, 0.0], [12.1518987342, 0.0], [13.164556962, 0.0], [14.1772151899, 0.0], [15.1898734177, 0.0], [16.2025316456, 0.0], [17.2151898734, 0.0], [18.2278481013, 0.0], [19.2405063291, 0.0], [20.253164557, 0.0], [21.2658227848, 0.0], [22.2784810127, 0.0], [23.2911392405, 0.0], [24.3037974684, 0.0], [25.3164556962, 0.0], [26.3291139241, 0.0], [27.3417721519, 0.0], [28.3544303797, 0.0], [29.3670886076, 0.0], [30.3797468354, 0.0], [31.3924050633, 0.0], [32.4050632911, 0.0], [33.417721519, 0.0], [34.4303797468, 0.0], [35.4430379747, 0.0], [36.4556962025, 0.0], [37.4683544304, 0.0], [38.4810126582, 0.0], [39.4936708861, 0.0], [40.5063291139, 0.0], [41.5189873418, 0.0], [42.5316455696, 0.0], [43.5443037975, 0.0], [44.5569620253, 0.0], [45.5696202532, 0.0], [46.582278481, 0.0], [47.5949367089, 0.0], [48.6075949367, 0.0], [49.6202531646, 0.0], [50.6329113924, 0.0], [51.6455696203, 0.0], [52.6582278481, 0.0], [53.6708860759, 0.0], [54.6835443038, 0.0], [55.6962025316, 0.0], [56.7088607595, 0.0], [57.7215189873, 0.0], [58.7341772152, 0.0], [59.746835443, 0.0], [60.7594936709, 0.0], [61.7721518987, 0.0], [62.7848101266, 0.0], [63.7974683544, 0.0], [64.8101265823, 0.0], [65.8227848101, 0.0], [66.835443038, 0.0], [67.8481012658, 0.0], [68.8607594937, 0.0], [69.8734177215, 0.0], [70.8860759494, 0.0], [71.8987341772, 0.0], [72.9113924051, 0.0], [73.9240506329, 0.0], [74.9367088608, 0.0], [75.9493670886, 0.0], [76.9620253165, 0.0], [77.9746835443, 0.0], [78.9873417722, 0.0], [80.0, 0.0]]
1854    """
1855    length_ = distance(line[0], line[1])
1856    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
1857    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
1858    increments = int(length_ / segment_length)
1859    x_segments = np.linspace(x1, x2, increments)
1860    y_segments = np.linspace(y1, y2, increments)
1861
1862    return list(zip(x_segments, y_segments))

1865def line_through_point_and_angle(
1866    point: PointType, angle: float, length_: float = 100
1867) -> LineType:
1868    """Return a line through the given point with the given angle and length
1869
1870    Args:
1871        point (PointType): PointType through which the line passes.
1872        angle (float): Angle of the line in radians.
1873        length_ (float, optional): Length of the line. Defaults to 100.
1874
1875    Returns:
1876        LineType: Line passing through the given point with the given angle and length.
1877
1878    Examples:
1879        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import line_through_point_and_angle
1880        >>> line_through_point_and_angle((0, 0), 0, 1)
1881        [[0, 0], [1.0, 0.0]]
1882    """
1883    x, y = point[:2]
1884    dx = length_ * cos(angle)
1885    dy = length_ * sin(angle)
1886    return [[x, y], [x + dx, y + dy]]
1887
1888
1889def rotate_line(
1890    line: LineType, angle: float, about: PointType = (0, 0)
1891) -> LineType:
1892    """Return a line rotated by ``angle`` about a point.
1893
1894    Args:
1895        line (LineType): Input line defined by two points.
1896        angle (float): Rotation angle in radians (counterclockwise).
1897        about (PointType): Pivot. Defaults to ``(0, 0)``.
1898
1899    Returns:
1900        LineType: Rotated line.
1901
1902    Examples:
1903        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1904        >>> p0, p1 = sg.rotate_line(
1905        ... [(100, 0), (200, 0)], sg.pi / 2, about=(0, 0)
1906        ... )
1907        >>> (round(p0[0], 10), round(p0[1], 10)), (
1908        ... round(p1[0], 10),
1909        ... round(p1[1], 10),
1910        ... )
1911        ((0.0, 100.0), (0.0, 200.0))
1912    """
1913    about_x, about_y = about[:2]
1914    cosine = cos(angle)
1915    sine = sin(angle)
1916    rotated = []
1917    for point in (line[0], line[1]):
1918        x, y = point[:2]
1919        delta_x = x - about_x
1920        delta_y = y - about_y
1921        rotated.append(
1922            [
1923                about_x + delta_x * cosine - delta_y * sine,
1924                about_y + delta_x * sine + delta_y * cosine,
1925            ]
1926        )
1927    return rotated
1928
1929
1930def translate_line(dx: float, dy: float, line: LineType) -> LineType:
1931    """Return a translated line by dx and dy
1932
1933    Args:
1934        dx (float): Translation distance in x-direction.
1935        dy (float): Translation distance in y-direction.
1936        line (LineType): Input line.
1937
1938    Returns:
1939        LineType: Translated line.
1940
1941    Examples:
1942        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import translate_line
1943        >>> translate_line(0, 1, [(0, 0), (40, 0)])
1944        [[0, 1], [40, 1]]
1945    """
1946    x1, y1 = line[0][:2]
1947    x2, y2 = line[1][:2]
1948    return [[x1 + dx, y1 + dy], [x2 + dx, y2 + dy]]
1949
1950
1951def _is_line_translate(value: object) -> bool:
1952    """Return True if ``value`` is a ``(dx, dy)`` pair."""
1953    if isinstance(value, Sequence) and not isinstance(value, (str, bytes)):
1954        if len(value) == 2:
1955            delta_x, delta_y = value
1956            return is_number(delta_x) and is_number(delta_y)
1957    return False
1958
1959
1960def _is_line_rotate(value: object) -> bool:
1961    """Return True if ``value`` is ``(angle, about)``."""
1962    if isinstance(value, Sequence) and not isinstance(value, (str, bytes)):
1963        if len(value) == 2:
1964            angle, about = value
1965            return is_number(angle) and is_point(about)
1966    return False
1967
1968
1969def update_line(line: LineType, incr: object) -> LineType:
1970    """Return a line after one increment, or after an ordered sequence of them.
1971
1972    A number is a perpendicular offset. ``(dx, dy)`` translates both
1973    endpoints. ``(angle, about)`` rotates about a point. A sequence of
1974    those steps is applied in the given order. ``(callable, arg)`` is
1975    resolved to one of the above.
1976
1977    Args:
1978        line (LineType): Input line defined by two points.
1979        incr: One increment, a sequence of increments, or
1980            ``(callable, arg)``.
1981
1982    Returns:
1983        LineType: The updated line.
1984
1985    Raises:
1986        TypeError: If ``incr`` is not a recognized line increment.
1987        ValueError: If ``incr`` is an empty sequence.
1988
1989    Examples:
1990        >>> import simetri.graphics as sg
1991        >>> sg.update_line([(0, 0), (100, 0)], 20)
1992        [[0.0, 20.0], [100.0, 20.0]]
1993        >>> sg.update_line([(0, 0), (100, 0)], (0, 20))
1994        [[0.0, 20.0], [100.0, 20.0]]
1995        >>> p0, p1 = sg.update_line(
1996        ... [(100, 0), (200, 0)], (sg.pi / 2, (0, 0))
1997        ... )
1998        >>> (round(p0[0], 10), round(p0[1], 10)), (
1999        ... round(p1[0], 10),
2000        ... round(p1[1], 10),
2001        ... )
2002        ((0.0, 100.0), (0.0, 200.0))
2003        >>> p0, p1 = sg.update_line(
2004        ... [(0, 0), (100, 0)], [(0, 20), (sg.pi / 2, (0, 0))]
2005        ... )
2006        >>> (round(p0[0], 10), round(p0[1], 10)), (
2007        ... round(p1[0], 10),
2008        ... round(p1[1], 10),
2009        ... )
2010        ((-20.0, 0.0), (-20.0, 100.0))
2011        >>> p0, p1 = sg.update_line(
2012        ... [(0, 0), (100, 0)], [(sg.pi / 2, (0, 0)), (0, 20)]
2013        ... )
2014        >>> (round(p0[0], 10), round(p0[1], 10)), (
2015        ... round(p1[0], 10),
2016        ... round(p1[1], 10),
2017        ... )
2018        ((0.0, 20.0), (0.0, 120.0))
2019    """
2020    if is_number(incr):
2021        return offset_line(line, float(incr))
2022    if isinstance(incr, Sequence) and not isinstance(incr, (str, bytes)):
2023        if (
2024            len(incr) == 2
2025            and callable(incr[0])
2026            and not _is_line_translate(incr)
2027        ):
2028            return update_line(line, incr[0](incr[1]))
2029        if _is_line_translate(incr):
2030            delta_x, delta_y = incr
2031            return translate_line(float(delta_x), float(delta_y), line)
2032        if _is_line_rotate(incr):
2033            angle, about = incr
2034            return rotate_line(line, float(angle), about)
2035        if len(incr) == 0:
2036            raise ValueError("incr is an empty sequence")
2037        updated = line
2038        for step in incr:
2039            if (
2040                is_number(step)
2041                or _is_line_translate(step)
2042                or _is_line_rotate(step)
2043            ):
2044                updated = update_line(updated, step)
2045            else:
2046                raise TypeError(
2047                    "Each line increment must be an offset, (dx, dy), "
2048                    f"or (angle, about); got {step!r}."
2049                )
2050        return updated
2051
2052    raise TypeError(
2053        "A line increment must be an offset, (dx, dy), (angle, about), "
2054        f"or a sequence of those; got {incr!r}."
2055    )
2056
2057
2058def trim_line(line1: LineType, line2: LineType) -> LineType:
2059    """Trim line1 to the intersection of line1 and line2.
2060    Extend it if necessary.
2061
2062    Args:
2063        line1 (LineType): First line.
2064        line2 (LineType): Second line.
2065
2066    Returns:
2067        LineType: Trimmed line.
2068
2069    Examples:
2070        >>> from simetri.base.all_enums import Connection
2071        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import trim_line
2072        >>> start, end = trim_line(((0, 0), (80, 0)), ((80, -40), (80, 40)))
2073        >>> start, end[0] == Connection.INTERSECT, end[1]
2074        ((0, 0), True, (80.0, 0.0))
2075    """
2076    intersection_ = intersection(line1, line2)
2077    return [line1[0], intersection_]
2078

2080def angle_between_two_lines(line1: LineType, line2: LineType) -> float:
2081    """Return the angle between two lines in radians.
2082
2083    Args:
2084        line1 (LineType): First line.
2085        line2 (LineType): Second line.
2086
2087    Returns:
2088        float: Angle between the two lines in radians.
2089
2090    Examples:
2091        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import angle_between_two_lines
2092        >>> angle_between_two_lines([(0, 0), (40, 0)], [(0, 0), (0, 40)])
2093        1.5707963267948966
2094    """
2095    alpha1 = line_angle(*line1)
2096    alpha2 = line_angle(*line2)
2097    return abs(alpha1 - alpha2)

2100def bisector_line3(a: PointType, b: PointType, c: PointType) -> LineType:
2101    """
2102    Given three points that form two lines [a, b] and [b, c]
2103    return the bisector line between them.
2104
2105    Args:
2106        a (PointType): First point.
2107        b (PointType): Second point.
2108        c (PointType): Third point.
2109
2110    Returns:
2111        LineType: Bisector line.
2112
2113    Examples:
2114        >>> from simetri.geom.segments.line_utils import bisector_line3
2115        >>> bisector_line3((0, 0), (40, 40), (80, 0))
2116        [(40.0, 0.0), (40, 40)]
2117    """
2118    d = midpoint(a, c)
2119
2120    return [d, b]
